source_quote: I spent the hour before the assault doing the thing that was useful and quiet and required no discussion.

source_quote: # Chapter 46 Fungus Among Us

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during the current planning session for the assassination of Ilvara, following the speaker’s continued observation of party dynamics, spore effects, and interpersonal tensions.
source_quote: We'd seen what happened when someone stopped worrying about them.

subject: session date
fact: The events occur during the current session, immediately following the planning phase and leading directly into the execution of the assassination plan.
source_quote: Now we just had to survive the execution.

subject: session date
fact: The events occur during the planning and execution of the assassination of Ilvara, following the party's arrival in the Underdark and their prior visit to the Whorlstone Caverns.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs during the Battle of the Heart Fungus.

subject: activation of the Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding inscribed on the bridge was triggered by Jorlan’s charge, killing one spore servant and severely damaging another, while also shuddering the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: The detonation is immediate and total — 21 damage, one spore servant gone to nothing...

subject: asha's assessment of allies
fact: I thought you had strong allies, who had a tactical awareness and understanding how to use their magic for destructive purposes.
source_quote: I thought you had strong allies, who had a tactical awareness and understanding how to use their magic for destructive purposes.

subject: Asha's belittling of belief
fact: Asha undermines her own authority by saying 'I believe' about the origin of Ilvara’s spore illness, revealing uncertainty where she previously claimed certainty.
source_quote: The particular spore illness only originates from Ilvara's spores and from her mushroom... I believe

subject: asha's demand
fact: The gratitude of Lolth.
source_quote: The gratitude of Lolth.

subject: Asha's emotional admission
fact: Asha reveals personal exasperation over Jorlan and Ilvara’s past affair and ongoing emotional entanglement, humanizing her beyond her contempt.
source_quote: They used to have an affair... now I've had to be in the middle of these two for the last few months... Do you have any idea how aggravating that is?

subject: asha's fear of contamination
fact: Don't touch me.
source_quote: Don't touch me.

subject: asha's hatred of ilvara
fact: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless. We need to kill her. We need to butcher her! We need to send her to an unearthly grave! I fear that her disease will spread.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless. We need to kill her. We need to butcher her! We need to send her to an unearthly grave! I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: asha's need for assistance
fact: I was not going to kill her. That is what you… where you come in.
source_quote: I was not going to kill her. That is what you… where you come in.

subject: asha's new theory
fact: Have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power? Is this another trick of Ilvara's?
source_quote: Have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power? Is this another trick of Ilvara's?

subject: asha's question
fact: You're a wizard. A wizard… a wizard who prays to Lolth?
source_quote: You're a wizard. A wizard… a wizard who prays to Lolth?

subject: Asha's revelation about captured drow
fact: Only Asha and Jorlan are no longer captured by Ilvara's spores — Asha due to devotion to Lolth, Jorlan due to hatred for Ilvara.
source_quote: The only three people who are no longer captured by her spores are myself and Jorlan... Me, because I have diligently kept the faith to Lolth... and Jorlan, because apparently he really hates Ilvara

subject: asha's suspicion
fact: You are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth, who are willing to believe every charlatan magic user that is somehow being possessed by the power of Lolth.
source_quote: You are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth, who are willing to believe every charlatan magic user that is somehow being possessed by the power of Lolth.

subject: asha's test
fact: This was just a test.
source_quote: This was just a test.

subject: Asha's Test of Daz
fact: Asha Vandree initiates a psychological test of Daz and his allies by accusing them of spore infection and questioning their devotion; her goal is to gauge their sincerity and identify whether they are trustworthy agents.
source_quote: This was just a test.

subject: Assassination Planning
fact: The party planned the assassination of Ilvara using Grygum’s limited 4th-level spell slots, debating whether to use Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, or Phantasmal Killer — each offering a different tactical advantage against a paranoid, fungal-corrupted target.
source_quote: Three keys. One lock. The planning was, in a sense, just a very elaborate way of deciding which door we most needed to open.

subject: battle escalation
fact: The battle has escalated with multiple attacks, critical hits, and environmental damage, changing the tactical math and increasing urgency.
source_quote: The math has changed. ... the fight rages in all directions around him.

subject: Battle of the Heart Fungus
fact: The Battle of the Heart Fungus began with Zalthir teleporting to Ilvara, triggering the Heart Fungus’s spore cloud, summoning spore servants, and culminating in Jorlan triggering the Glyph of Warding, allowing Thorin to engage in melee.
source_quote: The plan was always going to start without me... Zalthir vanish — just gone, teleported straight to her — and then there's the crack of his fists... The Heart Fungus has been sitting... unleashes a cloud of spores... Then the spore servants come up out of the ground... Jorlan charges... the detonation is immediate and total...

subject: damage event
fact: Five damage is dealt by a glancing strike.
source_quote: Five damage. A glancing thing.

subject: dancing lights shape
fact: Dancing Lights, shaped not into floating globes but into something grander — a silhouette, towering and feminine and terrible, the suggestion of eight eyes and infinite patience.
source_quote: Dancing Lights, shaped not into floating globes but into something grander — a silhouette, towering and feminine and terrible, the suggestion of eight eyes and infinite patience.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed Glabbagool was talking and moving despite being instructed to remain silent and motionless.
source_quote: I heard the reminder that invisible rocks do not speak. I heard — I am fairly certain I heard — the small wet sound of him opening his eyes, which then began tracking left and right with the particular energy of someone who absolutely cannot help himself.

subject: Daz's Revelation of Strategy
fact: Daz reveals that he and his allies are not specialists in fungal corruption but advocates of caution and preparation; this reframing shifts Asha’s perception of them from ignorant fools to deliberate strategists.
source_quote: Asking before blundering in was the sensible approach — not ignorance, caution.

subject: Fireball impact
fact: A Fireball centered on Ilvara and her mushroom icon deals 24 damage despite her saving throw.
source_quote: And then Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.

subject: fire damage event
fact: 24 damage worth of fire finds Ilvara even through her save.
source_quote: 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save

subject: force damage event
fact: Twenty force damage is delivered per turn by Grygum's action.
source_quote: delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise

subject: glabbagool talking
fact: Glabbagool started talking. I heard the reminder that invisible rocks do not speak. I heard — I am fairly certain I heard — the small wet sound of him opening his eyes, which then began tracking left and right with the particular energy of someone who absolutely cannot help himself.
source_quote: Glabbagool started talking. I heard the reminder that invisible rocks do not speak. I heard — I am fairly certain I heard — the small wet sound of him opening his eyes, which then began tracking left and right with the particular energy of someone who absolutely cannot help himself.

subject: glyph detonation
fact: Jorlan charges onto the Glyph of Warding, triggering a 21-damage explosion that destroys one spore servant, cripples another, and destabilizes the Heart Fungus — a decisive shift in battlefield dynamics.
source_quote: He comes straight onto the bridge, straight onto the glyph, and the detonation is immediate and total — 21 damage, one spore servant gone to nothing, another barely holding itself together, and the Heart Fungus itself shuddering from the force of it.

subject: Glyph inscription limitation
fact: The glyph cannot distinguish between hostile and non-hostile drow — it detonates on any who cross, forcing the party to use Jorlan as a trigger.
source_quote: I don't know how to inscribe a glyph that will only kill the drow that we don't like

subject: Glyph Inscription on the Bridge
fact: The party inscribed a lethal glyph on the bridge to control passage, using it as a tactical barrier. The inscription required greater force than wood, symbolizing the permanence and weight of their decision. The choice to target Jorlan’s side reflects a moral compromise — the glyph does not judge, but the party does.
source_quote: Stone holds runes differently than wood — you have to press harder, commit earlier.

subject: Glyph of Warding trigger
fact: The Glyph of Warding on the bridge detonates when Jorlan approaches from the side he is on, killing one spore servant and damaging the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: Jorlan charges... straight onto the glyph, and the detonation is immediate and total — 21 damage, one spore servant gone to nothing

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum decided to trigger the glyph against anyone approaching from Jorlan's side.
source_quote: Okay," I said. "And then, I guess the trigger is — anyone approaching from the side that Jorlan is on.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed that the mushroom artifact could exploit a marker left on him and Thorin from Gracklstugh.
source_quote: Whatever we'd picked up in Gracklstugh in the Whorlstone Caverns when we visited the pocket dimension, had left a marker on us. The mushroom artifact could exploit it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized he could only cast one of his three 4th-level spells due to having only one 4th-level slot.
source_quote: So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized the glyph would not distinguish between drow he liked and those he didn't.
source_quote: I don't know how to inscribe a glyph that will only kill the drow that we don't like.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized the spore servants were former drow who had made a choice to embrace Ilvara's power.
source_quote: People. Hollowed out. Not monsters dragged in from somewhere else, but people who had made a choice — a terrible choice, maybe a seduced choice — and were now walking around as the consequence of it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled the spell Dust of Suleiman and its effects.
source_quote: So I also have another spell I haven't had a chance to use yet called the Dust of Suleiman… It creates a 20-foot sphere, and anything inside this sphere takes 20 points of damage per turn.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled the spell Glyph of Warding and its triggering mechanism.
source_quote: It's a… the spell is Glyph of Warding… You inscribe it in a particular place, and then when somebody triggers it by moving across it, it does its thing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled the spell Phantasmal Killer and its mechanics.
source_quote: Finally, I now have Phantasmal Killer… It says you tap into the nightmares of a creature you can see and create an illusory manifestation of its deepest fears.

subject: grygum's spell limitation
fact: So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.
source_quote: So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.

subject: grygum's spells
fact: It's a… the spell is Glyph of Warding. You inscribe it in a particular place, and then when somebody triggers it by moving across it, it does its thing.
source_quote: It's a… the spell is Glyph of Warding. You inscribe it in a particular place, and then when somebody triggers it by moving across it, it does its thing.

subject: Heart Fungus grinding
fact: Grygum grinds the Heart Fungus, delivering twenty force damage per turn, causing it to shudder.
source_quote: Behind me, deeper in the cavern, Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise. The thing shudders. Good. Let it shudder.

subject: Inspection of the Glyph
fact: Grygum inscribed the Glyph of Warding on the bridge, acknowledging the moral dilemma that it cannot distinguish between friend and foe, and chose to trigger it on Jorlan's approach.
source_quote: I don't know how to inscribe a glyph that will only kill the drow that we don't like... Okay, and then, I guess the trigger is — anyone approaching from the side that Jorlan is on.

subject: Introduction of Glabbagool as a Familiar
fact: Glabbagool was introduced as Daz's familiar to explain his presence, and Asha's expression shifted from alarmed to impressed upon learning this, elevating Daz's perceived status.
source_quote: Asha considered this. Her expression shifted from alarmed to — and I watched this happen in real time — impressed. 'An ooze familiar,' she said, looking at Daz now with something approaching respect.

subject: Introduction of Glabbagool as a Familiar
fact: To conceal Glabbagool’s true nature as an ooze creature, Thorin introduces him as Daz’s familiar. Asha’s reaction shifts from alarm to impressed respect, altering the party’s perception of Daz and creating a moment of unspoken bonding through deception.
source_quote: An ooze familiar," she said, looking at Daz now with something approaching respect.

subject: Jorlan's Charge onto the Glyph
fact: Thorin lured Jorlan onto the Glyph of Warding by shouting 'Come get it, idiot!' causing a detonation that killed one spore servant and damaged the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: 'Come get it, idiot!' ... Jorlan charges. He comes straight onto the bridge, straight onto the glyph, and the detonation is immediate and total — 21 damage, one spore servant gone to nothing...

subject: Negotiation with Asha Vandree
fact: A negotiation occurred in which Daz’s illusion of Lolth’s possession was misinterpreted by Asha as a divine test of her discernment, leading her to reveal critical intelligence about Ilvara’s cult, spores, and the Heart Fungus, while remaining terrified of contamination.
source_quote: you are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth, who are willing to believe every charlatan magic user that is somehow being possessed by the power of Lolth.

subject: performance of divine communion
fact: The wizard performed an illusionary act of communion with Lolth using a spider and Dancing Lights, intending to deceive Asha Vandree into believing he was a vessel of the Spider Queen — but the performance was reinterpreted by Asha as a divine test, then as a fungal infection.
source_quote: I am… you are not speaking to the wizard of this body. I… he… this body has communed with Lolth. And I… I am speaking through this body.

subject: plan moving parts
fact: The plan had three moving parts.
source_quote: The plan had three moving parts.

subject: planning session for Ilvara's assassination
fact: The party convened to plan Ilvara’s assassination, debating which of Grygum’s three 4th-level spells to use and whom to target. Asha Vandree redirected the focus from Ilvara to the Heart Fungus as the strategic linchpin, altering the tactical priority of the mission.
source_quote: Three keys. One lock. The planning was, in a sense, just a very elaborate way of deciding which door we most needed to open.

subject: Revelation of Asha's Belief in Ilvara's Spore Origin
fact: Asha stated 'I believe' regarding the origin of the spore illness, undermining her authority and revealing uncertainty in what she had previously presented as fact.
source_quote: The particular spore illness only originates from Ilvara's spores and from her mushroom... I believe.

subject: Revelation of Asha's Emotional State
fact: Asha revealed genuine exasperation about Jorlan's unresolved romantic history with Ilvara, showing vulnerability and humanity inconsistent with her prior contempt for Grygum.
source_quote: I agree! ... Like, you would think that in the midst of the abyss with the demons, everyone could get over their relationship issues, but no, no, no, no, no — Jorlan still is complaining that Ilvara… Ilvara this and Ilvara that.

subject: spore walker attack
fact: A spore walker attacks Thorin, missing the first swing but connecting on the second for five damage.
source_quote: Then a spore walker climbs up behind me, because of course it does, and the first swing misses clean — the thing reaches up and just swings into nothing, which is the best that can be said about it — but the second one connects. Five damage. A glancing thing.

subject: Tactical Handoff of the Crossbow
fact: Grygum handed his light crossbow to Thorin to enable ranged contribution, recognizing that everyone needs a way to contribute when the fight starts.
source_quote: I can lend — I can lend you my light crossbow... I handed it over and hoped he wouldn't need it.

subject: teleport-grapple-drop
fact: Zalthir teleports into position, grapples Ilvara, and drops her into the Heart Fungus’s damage zone, initiating the core tactical sequence of the battle.
source_quote: Zalthir vanishes — just gone, teleported straight to her — and then there's the crack of his fists finding purchase, once, twice, thirty-one damage in the space of a breath.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin adjusts his footing.
source_quote: I adjust my footing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin notices that Ilvara is bleeding.
source_quote: Ilvara is bleeding.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin notices that the mushroom is burning.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin realizes that the math has changed.
source_quote: The math has changed.

subject: Thorin's tactical redirection
fact: Thorin redirects Jorlan’s rage toward the Glyph of Warding by provoking him with a taunt, turning Jorlan into an unwitting trigger for the trap.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot!... Jorlan charges... straight onto the glyph

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed Asha Vandree treated him as furniture, ignoring him entirely during the conversation.
source_quote: She filed me away and returned her eyes to Daz. Not a glance afterward. Not a word in my direction for the duration of the conversation.

subject: Zalthir's teleport and grapple
fact: Zalthir teleports to Ilvara, grapples her, and attempts to drop her into the Phantasmal Killer spell, initiating the final phase of the battle plan.
source_quote: I can try to grab Ilvara and drop her into that, such that you're hurting both of them

subject: Zalthir's teleport and grapple on Ilvara
fact: Zalthir teleported to Ilvara and successfully grappled her, initiating the final phase of the assassination plan by attempting to drop her into the Phantasmal Killer spell.
source_quote: Zalthir vanish — just gone, teleported straight to her — and then there's the crack of his fists finding purchase...

subject: Asha's Faction
fact: Asha Vandree leads a faction loyal to traditional Lolth worship, rejecting Ilvara’s marriage doctrine as blasphemy; they are isolated, paranoid about contamination, and rely on outsiders to eliminate threats they dare not confront directly.
source_quote: We need to kill her. We need to butcher her! We need to send her to an unearthly grave!

subject: Ilvara's Cult
fact: Ilvara is a former high priestess of Lolth who has become obsessed with the idea of Lolth being married, and now leads a fungal cult that transforms followers into mindless fungal creatures using spores, posing a spreading threat to the Underdark.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married... all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Ilvara's Cult
fact: Ilvara leads a cult that believes Lolth wishes to be married, and her followers have been transformed into mindless fungal creatures by spores; this movement is viewed as a heretical corruption by Asha Vandree and her faction.
source_quote: There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Ilvara's Cult
fact: Ilvara's cult consists of drow who have embraced her claim that she is Lolth’s further manifestation. They willingly accept her spores, experiencing ecstasy and transformation, and have become hollowed-out servants. They are not monsters, but former drow who made a choice — now walking corpses of their former selves.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... There were those who foolishly believed Ilvara's claims about how the bride was Lolth's further manifestation, and who embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them.

subject: Ilvara's Cult
fact: Ilvara, a high priestess, maintained control over the cavern through the Heart Fungus, which served as both a source of power and a vector for infection. Her operation relied on the artifact’s symbiotic relationship with spores and the spore-dependent ecosystem.
source_quote: Ilvara was a high priestess who had been running an operation in this cavern... the Heart Fungus itself wasn't the vector. The spores were Ilvara's. The artifact was the other risk.

subject: Ilvara's Cult
fact: Ilvara’s cult consists of drow who have embraced her heretical claims that she is Lolth’s further manifestation, and have willingly succumbed to her spores, becoming hollowed-out spore servants.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them.

subject: Lolth's Faithful
fact: Lolth’s faithful, represented by Asha, reject Ilvara’s heresy and maintain strict devotion to the Spider Queen, distinguishing themselves from those corrupted by the bride cult.
source_quote: I have diligently kept the faith to Lolth, and have rejected all of these claims of the bride heresy.

subject: Lolth's Followers
fact: Among Asha Vandree’s sect, true devotion to Lolth is defined by rigid, fear-based orthodoxy — rejecting any display of emotion or uncertainty as false, and viewing spiritual possession or fungal corruption as heresy or infection.
source_quote: That is not the kind of conviction a follower of Lolth shows.

subject: Lolth's followers
fact: Lolth's followers are a fractured group of devotees, some genuine, others charlatans, whose paranoia leads them to suspect all manifestations of the Spider Queen’s power as either deception or infection — making them extremely difficult to deceive or convince.
source_quote: you are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth, who are willing to believe every charlatan magic user that is somehow being possessed by the power of Lolth.

subject: Velkynvelve
fact: Velkynvelve was once a guard force now corrupted into spore servants, reanimated by Ilvara’s fungal influence to serve as frontline shock troops in the battle.
source_quote: Four of them, former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and wrong.

subject: Zuggtmoy's influence
fact: Zuggtmoy’s influence is perceived as a fungal madness that corrupts perception, causing victims to believe in false deities or divine visions — a threat that has redefined Asha Vandree’s interpretation of the wizard’s act from deception to infection.
source_quote: Have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy?

subject: Asha Vandree’s mental state
fact: Asha Vandree’s mental state is shaped by paranoid devotion to Lolth, where suspicion has become its own kind of faith, causing her to reinterpret deception as divine testing.
source_quote: the look of someone who has spent so long in paranoid devotion that suspicion has become its own kind of faith.

subject: Bridge
fact: The bridge is the threshold where the Glyph of Warding was inscribed, and where Jorlan was lured to trigger its detonation, shifting the tactical balance of the battle.
source_quote: Jorlan charges. He comes straight onto the bridge, straight onto the glyph, and the detonation is immediate and total — 21 damage, one spore servant gone to nothing...

subject: Bridge elevation
fact: The bridge where Grygum inscribed the Glyph of Warding becomes the critical threshold between the party and Ilvara’s forces.
source_quote: The glyph went down on the bridge... The bridge was now a threshold

subject: Bridge of the Glyph
fact: The bridge is a strategic chokepoint where Grygum inscribed a Glyph of Warding keyed to Jorlan’s approach, turning the structure into a lethal threshold for Ilvara’s allies.
source_quote: The glyph went down on the bridge... Everything on the far side of it was already committed to a detonation it didn't know about yet.

subject: Bridge of Warding
fact: The bridge spans a pit over the cavern, bearing the Glyph of Warding placed by Grygum — it is the focal point of the ambush, where Jorlan’s charge triggers the decisive tactical moment.
source_quote: Jorlan is standing exactly twenty feet from the Glyph of Warding that Grygum spent real patience setting into the stone of the bridge.

subject: Cavern of the Heart Fungus
fact: The cavern is a corrupted subterranean space dominated by the pulsing Heart Fungus, with elevated platforms, fungal growths, and hidden glyphs — terrain that is actively hostile and dynamically reshaped by Ilvara’s will.
source_quote: We watched Ilvara from the corridor near the pools... The cavern is full in a way that starts to feel personal.

subject: Daz’s inner state
fact: Daz’s inner state is described as having been reduced and reconstituted through a ritual involving a spider and luminous lights, culminating in the sensation of Lolth’s presence within him.
source_quote: The luminescence built. Condensed. The shape of the Spider Queen herself, reduced and reduced and *reduced* until it shrank into that small skittering body and seemed to pass directly into mine.

subject: fungal floor
fact: The spider scurried back across the fungal floor toward me on cue.
source_quote: The spider scurried back across the fungal floor toward me on cue.

subject: fungal shadows
fact: Behind me, somewhere in the fungal shadows, Glabbagool was doing what Glabbagool does.
source_quote: Behind me, somewhere in the fungal shadows, Glabbagool was doing what Glabbagool does.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is the location where the group visited a pocket dimension and acquired the mushroom artifact that leaves a marker on those who touched it.
source_quote: Whatever we'd picked up in Gracklstugh in the Whorlstone Caverns when we visited the pocket dimension, had left a marker on us.

subject: Gracklstugh marker
fact: The mushroom artifact from Gracklstugh in the Whorlstone Caverns left a detectable marker on the party, exploitable by the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: Whatever we'd picked up in Gracklstugh in the Whorlstone Caverns when we visited the pocket dimension, had left a marker on us

subject: Grygum's action location
fact: Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down deeper in the cavern with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman*.
source_quote: Behind me, deeper in the cavern, Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman*

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a massive, pulsing fungal entity at the center of Ilvara’s domain, serving as the structural anchor of her control over the cavern and its spore servants.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus pulsed between us and her, enormous and obscene, the mechanism of her control.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is burning.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is the mechanism of Ilvara's control over the whole area, and killing it dismantles the architecture of her power.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus was the key. That was her point, and she wasn't wrong. The fungus was how Ilvara kept control over the whole area. Kill the fungus and you don't just hurt Ilvara — you dismantle the architecture of her power.

subject: Heart Fungus elevation
fact: The Heart Fungus is an enormous, pulsing mechanism of control situated between the party and Ilvara on her elevated platform.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus pulsed between us and her, enormous and obscene, the mechanism of her control

subject: Jorlan's position
fact: Jorlan is still in front of Thorin.
source_quote: Jorlan is still in front of me

subject: The Bridge
fact: The bridge is a strategic chokepoint where the party inscribed a lethal glyph to control access. It is now a threshold between safety and detonation, symbolizing the moral boundaries the party has drawn — and the innocent drow who may cross it unknowingly.
source_quote: The glyph went down on the bridge... Everything on the far side of it was already committed to a detonation it didn't know about yet.

subject: The Cavern
fact: The cavern is a secluded, ancient site where Asha Vandree has been isolated for an extended period, waiting for a solution to Ilvara’s threat; its atmosphere is thick with spore residue and unspoken dread.
source_quote: She had been sitting in this cavern, waiting for a solution to walk through the door.

subject: the cavern
fact: The cavern is a subterranean stronghold controlled by Ilvara, infused with the Heart Fungus and spore-based infection. It contains hidden risks from past exposure in Gracklstugh’s Whorlstone Caverns, which left a detectable marker on certain individuals that the artifact can exploit.
source_quote: Whatever we'd picked up in Gracklstugh in the Whorlstone Caverns when we visited the pocket dimension, had left a marker on us. The mushroom artifact could exploit it.

subject: the fungal floor of the Underdark
fact: The fungal floor of the Underdark is the setting for the wizard’s performance, where the spider scurries and the Dancing Lights condense — a place of decay and magic where perception is unstable and spores may corrupt the mind.
source_quote: The spider scurried back across the fungal floor toward me on cue... The luminescence built. Condensed.

subject: Underdark cavern
fact: The Underdark cavern contains fungal growths, a gelatinous cube disguised as a rock, and a zone of Darkness placed behind the party’s position as a fallback.
source_quote: I placed a zone of Darkness behind our position — not at the entrance, not anywhere Ilvara might notice the edge of it and understand what was coming. Behind us. A fallback. A place to pull someone if the line broke.

subject: Underdark Cavern
fact: The cavern is a fungal-infested Underdark chamber where Asha has been isolated for an extended period, monitoring Ilvara’s cult, and where the party conducted their negotiation and planned their assault, with hidden zones of darkness prepared for retreat.
source_quote: I placed a zone of Darkness behind our position — not at the entrance, not anywhere Ilvara might notice the edge of it and understand what was coming. Behind us. A fallback.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: The drow outpost of Velkynvelve is referenced as the former home of the spore servants who were once its guards.
source_quote: four of them, former Velkynvelve guards

subject: Whorlstone Caverns
fact: The Whorlstone Caverns are the location where the group visited a pocket dimension and acquired the mushroom artifact that leaves a marker on those who touched it.
source_quote: Whatever we'd picked up in Gracklstugh in the Whorlstone Caverns when we visited the pocket dimension, had left a marker on us.

subject: Whorlstone Caverns marker
fact: The mushroom artifact from the Whorlstone Caverns left a marker on the party, exploitable by the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: Whatever we'd picked up in Gracklstugh in the Whorlstone Caverns when we visited the pocket dimension, had left a marker on us

subject: zone of darkness
fact: I placed a zone of Darkness behind our position — not at the entrance, not anywhere Ilvara might notice the edge of it and understand what was coming. Behind us. A fallback. A place to pull someone if the line broke.
source_quote: I placed a zone of Darkness behind our position — not at the entrance, not anywhere Ilvara might notice the edge of it and understand what was coming. Behind us. A fallback. A place to pull someone if the line broke.

subject: Zuggtmoy's influence
fact: Zuggtmoy’s influence is perceived as a source of fungal madness capable of infecting minds and causing hallucinations of divine presence.
source_quote: possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power?

subject: fireball target count
fact: Daz's Fireball catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center.
source_quote: Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous cube encountered as a hazardous companion who has failed to maintain concealment, actively disrupting a performance by speaking, moving, and exhibiting awareness — rendering him a liability rather than a prop.
source_quote: I heard the reminder that invisible rocks do not speak. I heard — I am fairly certain I heard — the small wet sound of him opening his eyes, which then began tracking left and right with the particular energy of someone who absolutely cannot help himself.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze familiar capable of forming articulate shapes and utterances, which is highly unusual for such a creature; Daz has established control over it, suggesting it is more sentient or magically bound than it appears.
source_quote: Glabbagool, I'm taking care of this, it's fine.

subject: Glabbagool classification
fact: Glabbagool, an ooze from the Whorlstone Caverns, is officially introduced as Daz's familiar to explain his presence.
source_quote: Thorin introduced Glabbagool as Daz's familiar

subject: glabbagool count
fact: Glabbagool was doing what Glabbagool does. Which is to say: failing at the very simple task of being a rock.
source_quote: Glabbagool was doing what Glabbagool does. Which is to say: failing at the very simple task of being a rock.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a powerful magical artifact associated with Ilvara’s cult, not itself the vector of infection but a dangerous relic that must be destroyed to prevent its power from spreading.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus itself wasn't the vector. The spores were Ilvara's. The artifact was the other risk.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a sentient, pulsing fungal entity that controls Ilvara, emits lethal spore clouds, and reforms her after damage — it acts as both a living mechanism and a hostile environmental hazard.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus pulsed between us and her, enormous and obscene, the mechanism of her control... It unleashes a cloud of spores that hits Zalthir so hard he has to climb ten feet straight up just to breathe.

subject: spider count
fact: A small spider, real enough, convincing enough if you don't look too hard at the absence of divine ichor.
source_quote: A small spider, real enough, convincing enough if you don't look too hard at the absence of divine ichor.

subject: spores
fact: The spores are the infectious agents directly controlled by Ilvara, released from the Heart Fungus and capable of propagating the infection. They are not the artifact itself but the biological vector, and their containment is critical to mission success.
source_quote: The spores were Ilvara's. The artifact was the other risk. Contain both and the job was done.

subject: spore servant classification
fact: Spore servants are former drow who embraced Ilvara’s claims about the bride being Lolth’s manifestation, and are now hollowed-out extensions of her power.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them

subject: spore servant count
fact: Four spore servants — former Velkynvelve guards who succumbed to Ilvara's power — emerge from the ground during the battle.
source_quote: Then the spore servants come up out of the ground — four of them, former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and wrong

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Spore Servants are former drow guards who have fully succumbed to Ilvara’s spores, now shambling, corrupted husks bound to her will and acting as frontline enforcers.
source_quote: Four of them, former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and wrong...

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Spore Servants are former drow of the party who have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power, embracing her claims about the bride being Lolth's manifestation and now exist as hollowed-out walking consequences.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... There were those who foolishly believed Ilvara's claims about how the bride was Lolth's further manifestation, and who embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them.

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Spore Servants are reanimated former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and corrupted by fungal growth, emerging from the ground to reinforce Ilvara’s defenses during combat.
source_quote: Four of them, former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and wrong.

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Spore servants are former drow who have been transformed by Ilvara’s spores into mindless, obedient creatures. They retain human form but lack agency. They are not summoned or created, but corrupted from within — making them tragically familiar and dangerous to the party’s own members.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power...

subject: spore walker
fact: A spore walker has climbed behind Thorin and missed its first attack, but connected with a 5-damage glancing strike.
source_quote: Then a spore walker climbs up behind me, because of course it does, and the first swing misses clean — the thing reaches up and just swings into nothing, which is the best that can be said about it — but the second one connects. Five damage.

subject: spore walker count
fact: A spore walker climbs up behind Thorin.
source_quote: Then a spore walker climbs up behind me

subject: Zuggtmoy's Spores
fact: The spores of Zuggtmoy are a fungal infection capable of inducing madness, delusions of divine connection, and physical transformation, and are feared as a contagious, mind-corrupting force in the Underdark.
source_quote: Have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy?

subject: Asha
fact: Asha advocated for targeting the Heart Fungus’s infrastructure over emotional or symbolic destruction — her strategic insight directly influenced the choice to use the Dust of Suleiman.
source_quote: because Asha was right and the infrastructure was more important than the satisfying image of Ilvara's nightmares eating her alive.

subject: Asha
fact: Asha is a drow who claims to have resisted Ilvara's spores through devotion to Lolth, but her statements are undermined by her use of 'I believe,' indicating uncertainty rather than knowledge. She refuses to speak directly to the speaker after losing respect for them. She is exasperated by the unresolved romantic history between Jorlan and Ilvara, and is momentarily impressed by Daz's ooze familiar.
source_quote: My dear boy... Tell the Dragonborn that the big heart fungus will not actually cause any fungal disease, other than the usual poisoning and pain and suffering and breathing difficulties. The particular spore illness only originates from Ilvara's spores and from her mushroom. I believe.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree admits she cannot approach Ilvara herself due to fear of contamination and requires Daz and his allies to carry out the assassination.
source_quote: I was not going to kill her. That is what you… where you come in.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree flinches at physical contact, revealing a deep, personal fear of fungal contamination from prolonged exposure to Zuggtmoy’s influence.
source_quote: Don't touch me.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a drow priestess of Lolth who holds tactical authority over the operation against Ilvara, dismissive of Grygum but correct about the Heart Fungus being the key to dismantling Ilvara’s power structure.
source_quote: I thought you had strong allies, who had a tactical awareness and understanding how to use their magic for destructive purposes.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a drow who has been exposed to Zuggtmoy's spores and fears contamination; she is desperate for others to kill Ilvara because she cannot risk close proximity to the spores, and she views Ilvara’s devotion to a 'married Lolth' as a heretical abomination.
source_quote: I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a paranoid devotee of Lolth who has reframed the wizard's deception as a divine test of her discernment, believing herself to have passed it, and later suspects the wizard and his familiar are infected by Zuggtmoy's spores rather than deceived or divinely touched.
source_quote: Aha, you are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth, who are willing to believe every charlatan magic user that is somehow being possessed by the power of Lolth.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a paranoid, fanatically devoted follower of Lolth who believes Ilvara is corrupted by Zuggtmoy’s spores, and who misinterpreted Daz’s illusion as a divine trial — ultimately revealing critical intelligence about Ilvara’s operations while remaining terrified of contamination.
source_quote: Have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power? Is this another trick of Ilvara's?

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is referenced by Grygum as the authority who decided the fate of failed Drow, and whose territory was the politics of this cavern and the hierarchy of what needed to die in what order to make the rest of it possible.
source_quote: The politics of this cavern — the power structures, the hierarchy of what needed to die in what order to make the rest of it possible — that was Asha Vandree's territory, and I knew it.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree later reinterprets the spider, lights, and reverence as signs of fungal infection by Zuggtmoy, questioning whether Daz is a victim rather than a deceiver.
source_quote: have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power? Is this another trick of Ilvara's?

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree reveals that Ilvara, once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by the idea that Lolth wishes to be married and now spreads fungal corruption, turning allies into mindless fungal creatures.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree suspects Daz of being a charlatan but reframes his deception as a divine test of her discernment, believing she has passed and that Daz is a genuine follower of Lolth.
source_quote: you are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth, who are willing to believe every charlatan magic user that is somehow being possessed by the power of Lolth.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree, a contemptuous drow priestess, corrected Grygum’s tactical assumptions by identifying the Heart Fungus as the true key to dismantling Ilvara’s power. She warned that Grygum and Thorin were contaminated by a marker from Gracklstugh and should avoid direct contact with the artifact. She dismissed his initial focus on Ilvara as naive.
source_quote: Well, that's an obvious one — use it on the big heart fungus... If Thorin and Grygum grab it — I think they were the two that went to visit... you two probably don't want to be near it... I thought you had strong allies, who had a tactical awareness and understanding how to use their magic for destructive purposes.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz asserts that his conviction as a follower of Lolth is genuine and unique to him, rejecting Asha’s assumption that his behavior deviates from orthodox worship.
source_quote: It's the kind of conviction this follower of Lolth shows.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed conviction carries what evidence cannot if committed to fully enough.
source_quote: Conviction carries what evidence cannot, if you commit to it fully enough.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed he had convinced others to join him.
source_quote: I've convinced others to join me.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed his conviction was the kind this follower of Lolth shows.
source_quote: It's the kind of conviction this follower of Lolth shows.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz claims to have convinced others to join him in his mission, implying a network of followers who believe in his divine connection.
source_quote: I've convinced others to join me.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz coordinates the tactical phases of the battle — opening volley, spell depletion, brawler entry — and later executes a fireball to strike the overlap zone, demonstrating battlefield awareness and timing.
source_quote: Daz talked through the phases — the opening volley, the depletion of spell slots, the point at which the brawlers would need to go in... Daz fireballs the overlap.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt the specific sensation of a gamble that could go either way.
source_quote: I felt, for a fraction of a second, the specific sensation of a gamble that could go either way.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz has cast a precisely shaped Fireball that caught Ilvara and her mushroom icon in the center, dealing 24 damage despite her save.
source_quote: And then Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a Dragonborn who has been infected by Ilvara's spores, serving as a visual warning to the party, and is credited with securing Glabbagool as an ooze familiar, earning Asha’s reluctant respect.
source_quote: Look at him! He's already infected. I don't want to be infected.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a member of the party who listened attentively to Grygum’s spell explanations and showed engagement by asking clarifying questions, particularly about Phantasmal Killer. He is not a spellcaster but serves as an observer and sounding board.
source_quote: Daz was paying attention. I could tell... 'What's that?' Daz said. 'Sounds fantastic.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a surface-trained drow who manipulates perception by feigning sincere doubt and internalized spore infection to gain Asha Vandree’s trust; he operates with calculated boldness that blurs the line between foolishness and mastery.
source_quote: It's the kind of conviction this follower of Lolth shows.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a surface-trained illusionist who has performed a con involving a spider and Dancing Lights to impersonate a vessel of Lolth, successfully manipulating Asha Vandree by reframing his deception as a divine test she passed.
source_quote: I am… you are not speaking to the wizard of this body. I… he… this body has communed with Lolth. And I… I am speaking through this body.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a wizard who has communed with Lolth and speaks through his body, claiming to have been reduced to a small spider and then reconstituted, anchoring his claim in the observable presence of the spider.
source_quote: I am… you are not speaking to the wizard of this body. I… he… this body has communed with Lolth. And I… I am speaking through this body.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is infected by Ilvara's spores but remains coherent and rational, serving as a visual proof of the spores' effects. He is the familiar of Glabbagool, an ooze creature mistaken for a mundane familiar by the party to explain its presence. His calm demeanor and tactical insight earn Asha’s respect, despite his condition.
source_quote: I mean, — look at him! He's already infected. I don't want to be infected.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is visibly infected by spores, serving as a visual aid that the spores are not theoretical but a real and present danger.
source_quote: Zalthir gestured toward Daz. 'I mean, — look at him! He's already infected. I don't want to be infected.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz knows what he's doing.
source_quote: I know what I'm doing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.
source_quote: And then Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was pleased with his redirect to anchor the claim in the observable spider.
source_quote: A deft redirect — I was pleased with it — anchoring the claim in observable fact rather than asking her to simply take my word for a goddess.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous cube acting as a familiar who failed to remain inert during a critical negotiation, speaking and moving in ways that threatened the illusion — yet was dismissed by Asha as eccentricity of a spore-addled convert.
source_quote: Glabbagool, I'm taking care of this, it's fine.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous cube who has failed at the simple task of remaining motionless and silent as a cavern feature, instead talking, opening his eyes, and tracking movement — thereby disrupting the wizard's performance and revealing his inability to play the role of a rock.
source_quote: I heard the reminder that invisible rocks do not speak. I heard — I am fairly certain I heard — the small wet sound of him opening his eyes, which then began tracking left and right with the particular energy of someone who absolutely cannot help himself.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze creature that emerged from the dungeon ooze. To avoid suspicion, Thorin introduces him as Daz’s familiar. He blinks but appears indifferent to the mislabeling. The party recognizes the indignity of his treatment and notes he deserves something for enduring it.
source_quote: Will Glabbagool be offended if we refer to him as a familiar? I think that's probably the easiest way to just explain it away.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is described as failing at the simple task of being a rock, having been given clear instructions to remain motionless and silent.
source_quote: Glabbagool was doing what Glabbagool does. Which is to say: failing at the very simple task of being a rock.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a gelatinous cube meant to be an inanimate familiar, attempts to form an utterance during negotiation, nearly exposing the deception.
source_quote: The ooze had, apparently, opinions about the negotiation. It began to form the shape of an utterance — which is not something you want from what is supposed to be an inanimate ooze familiar.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed Asha's statement 'I believe' was less authoritative than a claim of knowledge.
source_quote: I believe. Two words that undermined everything she'd just said with such authority. I stored them carefully. *She believes.* Not *she knows.*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed some fears are just.
source_quote: Bahamut didn't teach me that one, exactly, but I don't think he'd object. Some fears are just.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the Dust of Suleiman should be used on the Heart Fungus because Asha was right.
source_quote: I took notes on the whole plan, the way I always do. Not on paper. In my head. Every piece placed, every spell accounted for. The Dust of Suleiman on the fungus, because Asha was right and the infrastructure was more important than the satisfying image of Ilvara's nightmares eating her alive.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum describes Glyph of Warding as a spell inscribed in a location that triggers when a creature moves across it, executing its effect automatically.
source_quote: It's a… the spell is Glyph of Warding… You inscribe it in a particular place, and then when somebody triggers it by moving across it, it does its thing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum describes Phantasmal Killer as a spell that taps into a creature’s deepest fears, creating an illusory manifestation that can cause 4d10 psychic damage if the target fails consecutive Wisdom saving throws.
source_quote: It says you tap into the nightmares of a creature you can see and create an illusory manifestation of its deepest fears. They become frightened if they fail a wisdom saving throw, and if they fail the saving throw in each turn — and it can last up to a minute — then they take 4 die 10 psychic damage.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum explains that Dust of Suleiman creates a 20-foot sphere at 120-foot range that deals 20 points of damage per turn to anything inside it.
source_quote: Which I can cast at a 120-foot distance. It creates a 20-foot sphere, and anything inside this sphere takes 20 points of damage per turn.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum felt it was not the most comfortable thing he'd done in the Underdark to ask Asha for tactical input.
source_quote: Asking a contemptuous drow priestess for tactical input is not the most comfortable thing I've done in the Underdark.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum felt the sting of being corrected by Asha, and feared she might be right.
source_quote: There it is. The sting of being corrected by someone who hates you — made worse by the possibility that she's right.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum hated it when Asha was right.
source_quote: She was right. I hate when that happens.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a spellcaster who presented three powerful 4th-level spells — Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, and Phantasmal Killer — but revealed he can only cast one due to limited spell slots, forcing the group to prioritize their approach to assassinating Ilvara.
source_quote: So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with a sound resembling 'Suleiman,' delivering 20 force damage per turn.
source_quote: Behind me, deeper in the cavern, Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise. The thing shudders.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise.
source_quote: Behind me, deeper in the cavern, Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise. The thing shudders. Good. Let it shudder.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is not too proud to ask for help when the terrain is unfamiliar.
source_quote: I'm not too proud to ask for help when the terrain is unfamiliar.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is planning the assassination of Ilvara, having deferred to Asha's tactical expertise despite her contempt, and has internalized critical intelligence about the Heart Fungus as infrastructure rather than a mere target.
source_quote: I took the note. I filed it. I did not say anything I would regret.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by Asha as the authority who decided to use the Dust of Suleiman on the Heart Fungus rather than on Ilvara directly, based on Asha's tactical insight.
source_quote: I took the note. I filed it. I did not say anything I would regret.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum knew the politics of the cavern were Asha Vandree's territory.
source_quote: The politics of this cavern — the power structures, the hierarchy of what needed to die in what order to make the rest of it possible — that was Asha Vandree's territory, and I knew it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum laid out the plan to assassinate Ilvara, detailing three 4th-level spells: Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, and Phantasmal Killer. He admitted he only had one 4th-level spell slot and could cast only one. He sought Asha Vandree’s tactical input on which target to prioritize.
source_quote: So I also have another spell I haven't had a chance to use yet called the Dust of Suleiman... Finally, I now have Phantasmal Killer... So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum placed the Glyph of Warding on the bridge with deliberate patience, creating a hidden tactical trap that becomes instrumental in disrupting Ilvara’s reinforcements.
source_quote: Jorlan is standing exactly twenty feet from the Glyph of Warding that Grygum spent real patience setting into the stone of the bridge.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum remembered that they had picked Asha over Jorlan.
source_quote: And I remember that we had picked Asha over Jorlan.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum reveals he possesses three 4th-level spells — Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, and Phantasmal Killer — but only one 4th-level spell slot, forcing a critical choice among them.
source_quote: So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought Glabbagool deserved something for the indignity of being called a familiar.
source_quote: I made a mental note that if we survived this, Glabbagool deserved something for the indignity of being called a familiar, even if he didn't seem to mind.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum took notes on Asha, recognizing her as more human than he'd given her credit for.
source_quote: I took notes. Not on the tactics — on Asha, who was more person than I'd given her credit for, even if she refused to speak to me directly.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara has been struck by Daz’s Fireball, taking 24 damage, her mushroom icon smolders, and she is now bleeding.
source_quote: the icon smolders. The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is bleeding.
source_quote: Ilvara is bleeding.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is bleeding. The mushroom icon she carries is smoldering after taking 24 damage from a Fireball.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is corrupted by fungal growth, preoccupied with the mushroom token, and her power is sustained by the Heart Fungus, which she uses to control the entire area.
source_quote: She was on an elevated platform. Corrupted. The fungal growth had changed her in ways that were specific and terrible — the scourge still in her hand, but everything else altered. She was preoccupied with the mushroom token.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara was once a high priestess of Lolth but has become obsessed with the idea that Lolth wishes to be married, spreading fungal corruption and turning followers into mindless fungal creatures.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a drow who has resisted Ilvara's spores because he hates her, reportedly due to a broken romantic relationship. He is not trusted by the party, and the glyph on the bridge is triggered to kill anyone approaching from his side. He is emotionally fixated on Ilvara, still complaining about her even amid the chaos of the Abyss.
source_quote: The only three people who are no longer captured by her spores are myself and Jorlan... Me, because I have diligently kept the faith to Lolth, and have rejected all of these claims of the bride heresy, and Jorlan, because apparently he really hates Ilvara for something or other.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a former lover of Ilvara, now bitter and estranged, whose emotional vulnerability was exploited by Thorin to trigger the Glyph of Warding on the bridge.
source_quote: Jorlan still is complaining that Ilvara… Ilvara this and Ilvara that.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a humiliated former follower of Ilvara, consumed by rage, standing directly on the Glyph of Warding unaware — his predictable emotional vector is exploited by Thorin to trigger a decisive area denial effect.
source_quote: He's across the cavern, bitter-eyed, nursing whatever wound his pride has taken since Ilvara discarded him.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is one of only three people no longer captured by Ilvara's spores, because he hates Ilvara for something or other, and was once in an affair with her.
source_quote: The only three people who are no longer captured by her spores are myself and Jorlan... I mean, they used to have an affair, it used to be this whole thing, and then she broke up with him, and then he was bitter because she broke up with him.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is staggered but not broken, still angry, and remains a threat with AC 18 after dodging a 2-roll attack.
source_quote: Jorlan staggers. He doesn't fall. ... Jorlan is still there, staggered but not broken, which means he's still angry, which means we are not done here.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is still in front of Thorin.
source_quote: Jorlan is still in front of me, and Dawnbringer is still in my hand.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin adjusts his footing.
source_quote: I adjust my footing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin decided to provoke Jorlan into triggering the glyph by shouting at him.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot!

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt a familiar surge of wanting to be in the middle of the fight.
source_quote: I note it, feel the familiar surge of wanting to be in the middle of it, and then she melts.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf brawler who accepts ranged roles out of necessity, wields a crossbow reluctantly, and holds Dawnbringer as his true weapon; he respects tactical leverage and operates through terrain and position.
source_quote: I'm standing on a bridge over a pit that smells like the inside of a dying thing... I take it, because I'd rather be in the fight badly than out of it entirely.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf brawler who adapted to the ranged nature of the battle by accepting a crossbow and manipulated Jorlan’s rage to activate the Glyph of Warding, turning emotional history into tactical advantage.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot!

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a member of the party who, along with Grygum, visited a prior location (Gracklstugh) and was marked by its lingering magic. Asha explicitly warned him and Grygum against touching the artifact due to contamination risk.
source_quote: If Thorin and Grygum grab it — I think they were the two that went to visit... you two probably don't want to be near it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is currently engaged in battle against Jorlan after landing a 14-damage hit that imposed disadvantage, and is now repositioning after a missed attack.
source_quote: The first hit lands true. Fourteen damage, and I roll through the Sap, put him off-balance, give him disadvantage on whatever's coming back at me.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the dwarf who pragmatically solves the problem of Glabbagool’s identity by labeling him as Daz’s familiar. His practicality defuses tension and demonstrates his role as the party’s problem-solver in moments of crisis.
source_quote: Will Glabbagool be offended if we refer to him as a familiar? I think that's probably the easiest way to just explain it away.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the son of the Ember Vanguard, flanked by a dead man's fungal corpse while the fight rages in all directions around him.
source_quote: Then a spore walker climbs up behind me, because of course it does, and the first swing misses clean — the thing reaches up and just swings into nothing, which is the best that can be said about it — but the second one connects. Five damage. A glancing thing. Thorin, son of the Ember Vanguard, flanked by a dead man's fungal corpse while the fight rages in all directions around him.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin knew his relationship to range was limited, shaped by being raised by giants.
source_quote: I'm a dwarf who was raised by giants, which means my relationship to range is 'how far can I throw this rock.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin made peace with the fact that the plan would start without him.
source_quote: The plan was always going to start without me. That's not self-pity — that's just terrain.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin reflects that being flanked by a dead man's fungal corpse while the fight rages around him is the best that can be said about the situation.
source_quote: Thorin, son of the Ember Vanguard, flanked by a dead man's fungal corpse while the fight rages in all directions around him.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin respected Ilvara's speed and adaptability, even though he didn't like it.
source_quote: She's fast. I respect it. I don't like it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thought Jorlan was predictable because his rage was personal and had a clear vector.
source_quote: Jorlan is a man who has been humiliated by someone he loved, left broken on the far side of that love, and he's been stewing in it so long the rot has gone all the way through. That makes him predictable. Rage that personal has a vector.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin was given Grygum's light crossbow to compensate for his lack of ranged capability, and used it to hold the line before engaging Jorlan in melee with Dawnbringer.
source_quote: I can lend — I can lend you my light crossbow... I took it, because I'd rather be in the fight badly than out of it entirely... Now I have Dawnbringer in hand...

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin was surprised the plan worked as cleanly as it did.
source_quote: I didn't expect it to work that cleanly. I'll take it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wishes the Heart Fungus would shudder.
source_quote: The thing shudders. Good. Let it shudder.

subject: Thorin, son of the Ember Vanguard
fact: Thorin is flanked by a dead man's fungal corpse during the ongoing battle, and has adjusted his footing after the spore walker's attack.
source_quote: Thorin, son of the Ember Vanguard, flanked by a dead man's fungal corpse while the fight rages in all directions around him. I adjust my footing.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed Asha Vandree's hatred and theology were wound together tightly.
source_quote: Hatred and theology, wound together so tightly you couldn't separate one from the other.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed every word of Asha Vandree's conviction about Ilvara.
source_quote: I believed every word of it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir executes the pivotal teleport-and-grapple maneuver to drop Ilvara into the Heart Fungus's damage zone, demonstrating precision and control over battlefield geometry.
source_quote: I can try to grab Ilvara and drop her into that, such that you're hurting both of them, and then the rest of you can fireball or whatever from there.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a drow who observed the entire negotiation in silence, treated as invisible by Asha Vandree, and used his drow-trained patience to gather intelligence, noting tactical details and emotional undercurrents without drawing attention.
source_quote: She filed me away and returned her eyes to Daz. Not a glance afterward. Not a word in my direction for the duration of the conversation.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a drow who recognizes and is deeply affected by the silent erasure of drow social warfare — the deliberate treatment of a person as furniture — and reflects on its enduring emotional weight.
source_quote: There is a particular kind of silence that drow society uses as a weapon... I have spent enough time among my own kind to recognise it immediately. It never gets easier to absorb.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a member of the party who raised concerns about spore contamination and proposed the final tactical sequence involving grappling Ilvara into the Phantasmal Killer spell.
source_quote: I can try to grab Ilvara and drop her into that, such that you're hurting both of them, and then the rest of you can fireball or whatever from there.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the observer and narrator, a drow who remains silent and unacknowledged by Asha Vandree; they meticulously document social dynamics, deception, and hidden intelligence, recognizing Asha’s verbal disclosures as a map of Ilvara’s infection vectors.
source_quote: I filed it away in the archive of things I have witnessed that I will never be able to explain.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knew the silence of deliberate erasure used by drow society and recognized it immediately.
source_quote: I have spent enough time among my own kind to recognise it immediately.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knew where the shadows fell in the cavern ahead and knew the shape of what they were walking into.
source_quote: I knew where the shadows fell in the cavern ahead. I knew the shape of what we were walking into.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted Asha Vandree's fear of contamination as earned and personal.
source_quote: Whatever confidence she projected, whatever command she assumed over the conversation, Asha Vandree was afraid of contamination in a very specific and personal way.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted that Daz was operating in a register of boldness indistinguishable from foolishness until it worked.
source_quote: There is a specific kind of bold that is indistinguishable from foolishness until it works, and then it looks like mastery.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir notes that Daz’s response to Asha’s fungal infection theory — 'I really do believe that I have' — used hesitation as texture to make conviction feel lived-in and authentic.
source_quote: I really do believe that I have. Perhaps there are some spores within me, but I… it feels… I feel it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observes that Asha Vandree treats him as invisible furniture during negotiations, addressing all questions and demands solely to Daz despite his physical presence.
source_quote: She filed me away and returned her eyes to Daz. Not a glance afterward. Not a word in my direction for the duration of the conversation.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir raised the broader concern about spores and proposed the final tactical plan to teleport into Ilvara, grapple her, and drop her into the area of effect of the Dust of Suleiman.
source_quote: Zalthir, bless him, raised the broader concern about spores. He'd been thinking about it — we all had. 'I can try to grab Ilvara and drop her into that, such that you're hurting both of them, and then the rest of you can fireball or whatever from there.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir withdrew to confer and confirmed the terms: Ilvara must die, the mushroom artifact must be destroyed, and the infection must not leave the cavern. He placed a zone of Darkness behind their position as a fallback, not near the entrance where Ilvara might detect it.
source_quote: I placed a zone of Darkness behind our position — not at the entrance, not anywhere Ilvara might notice the edge of it and understand what was coming. Behind us. A fallback. A place to pull someone if the line broke.

subject: Dancing Lights
fact: The Dancing Lights are an illusion shaped into the silhouette of the Spider Queen, used to create the impression of divine presence, and later integrated into the spider’s form to reinforce the illusion’s authenticity.
source_quote: I was already weaving the lights around it — not frantically... but with the quiet precision of someone who has thought this through to the fourth step.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is Thorin’s enchanted sword, a weapon of radiant light that defies the darkness of the cavern, wielded only when Thorin closes to melee — it symbolizes his true role as a frontline warrior.
source_quote: I have Dawnbringer in hand — the real hand, the right hand, the one that knows what it's doing... The blade catches some ambient light... and turns it into something brighter, something that has no business existing this deep underground.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is still in Thorin's hand.
source_quote: Jorlan is still in front of me, and Dawnbringer is still in my hand.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer remains in Thorin’s hand as the battle continues, unchanged and ready.
source_quote: Jorlan is still in front of me, and Dawnbringer is still in my hand.

subject: Dawnbringer possession
fact: Dawnbringer is still in Thorin's hand.
source_quote: Dawnbringer is still in my hand

subject: Dawnbringer value
fact: Dawnbringer is Thorin’s primary melee weapon, used to engage Jorlan after the glyph detonates, despite its limited effectiveness against high AC.
source_quote: Now I have Dawnbringer in hand... The blade catches some ambient light... and I close the distance

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: A 4th-level spell that creates a 20-foot sphere of damaging dust at 120-foot range, dealing 20 points of damage per turn to anything inside. Originally intended for direct use on Ilvara, it was reclassified by Asha as a tool for infrastructure demolition against the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: It creates a 20-foot sphere, and anything inside this sphere takes 20 points of damage per turn.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: Dust of Suleiman is a 4th-level spell that creates a 20-foot sphere dealing 20 points of damage per turn to all creatures within, usable from 120 feet away, and considered for use in the assassination of Ilvara.
source_quote: It creates a 20-foot sphere, and anything inside this sphere takes 20 points of damage per turn.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is a magical substance originally intended for direct use against Ilvara, but reclassified by Asha as superior for infrastructure demolition — specifically, to destroy the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman... was actually more valuable as infrastructure demolition.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is a magical substance used to burn the Heart Fungus, targeting its control infrastructure rather than Ilvara’s illusions — chosen for strategic efficacy over emotional satisfaction.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman burns the Heart Fungus... because Asha was right and the infrastructure was more important than the satisfying image of Ilvara's nightmares eating her alive.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman was originally imagined to be poured directly on Ilvara, but was later recognized as more valuable as infrastructure demolition targeting the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman, which I had been imagining pouring down on Ilvara directly, was actually more valuable as infrastructure demolition.

subject: dust of suleiman
fact: Which I can cast at a 120-foot distance. It creates a 20-foot sphere, and anything inside this sphere takes 20 points of damage per turn.
source_quote: Which I can cast at a 120-foot distance. It creates a 20-foot sphere, and anything inside this sphere takes 20 points of damage per turn.

subject: Dust of Suleiman value
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is more valuable as infrastructure demolition than as a direct weapon against Ilvara.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman, which I had been imagining pouring down on Ilvara directly, was actually more valuable as infrastructure demolition

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze creature presented as Daz’s familiar, whose unnatural presence impressed Asha and provided a cover story to avoid suspicion during the infiltration.
source_quote: An ooze familiar," she said, looking at Daz now with something approaching respect.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze that was introduced as Daz's familiar to explain its presence, despite being a sentient entity capable of blinking and not minding the mislabeling.
source_quote: Thorin solved it with characteristic practicality. 'Will Glabbagool be offended if we refer to him as a familiar? I think that's probably the easiest way to just explain it away,' he muttered. Then the dwarf introduced Glabbagool as Daz's familiar.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: Glyph of Warding is a 4th-level spell that can be inscribed on a surface or object and triggered by movement or action, used in planning to ambush Ilvara without direct confrontation.
source_quote: You inscribe it in a particular place, and then when somebody triggers it by moving across it, it does its thing.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding is a hidden magical trap placed by Grygum on the bridge, designed to detonate when triggered — it is the key tactical element that disrupts Ilvara’s reinforcement strategy.
source_quote: Jorlan is standing exactly twenty feet from the Glyph of Warding that Grygum spent real patience setting into the stone of the bridge.

subject: Glyph of Warding
